audit_result.proof_trace: `float::int_div(collateral_amount, exchange_rate)` performs floor integer division; when `exchange_rate > collateral_amount` (in decimal terms), the result is 0. The only guard is `assert!(collateral_amount > 0)` at line 157, but there is no post-computation `assert!(mint_amount > 0)`. `deposit_underlying(coin)` consumes the user's coin before the zero cToken balance is returned, causing permanent fund loss. The TODO comment at line 159 explicitly acknowledges this rounding risk without mitigation.
audit_result.attack_scenario: In a mature pool where exchange_rate > 1.0 (normal after any interest accrual), an attacker or honest user calls `deposit` with `collateral_amount` less than the current exchange_rate in raw token units; `mint_amount = 0` is computed, the deposited coin is transferred to the reserve, and 0 cTokens are returned — the user loses their deposit while all existing cToken holders benefit.

PROP-01b-partial1-inv-005.text: Mint operation must produce mint_amount > 0 when coin.value > 0.
